σαγγαικόν.definition: dub. sens., Roussel Cultes Égyptiens p.224

σάθων.definition: from like from a coaxing word of nurses to a boy-baby, Telecl.65

σάκκος.definition: or v. sub fin.:—coarse cloth of hair; anything made of this cloth

σάκος.definition: Ion. gen. Hes.Sc.334; metaph., shield, defence, A.Supp.190

σάλπη.definition: a sea-fish, the saupe, Box salpa, Epich.63, Arist.HA543a8, al. : also Archipp.19; is v.l. in Arist.HA534a16; ib.534a9, 621b7; ib.543a8

σάμαξ.definition: rush-mat, used as a bed in war, Chionid.1; also, = Lysipp.10

σάνδανον.definition: perh. sandal-wood, Santalum album, in pl., Aët.16.142

σανίς.definition: board, plank, timber; wooden platform, scaffold, or stage, Od.21.51

σάραπις.definition: or a white Persian robe with purple stripes, Democr.Eph.1, Ctes.Fr.43

σάρι.definition: pl. an Egyptian water-plant, Cyperus auricomus, Thphr.HP4.8.5: called saripha in Plin.HN13.128

σάρισα.definition: sarissa, a long pike used in the Macedonian phalanx, Thphr.HP3.12.2, Plb.2.69.9, 18.29.2, etc

σάτον.definition: a Hebrew measure, 1/30 of a = about a modius and a half or 24 sextarii, LXXHg.2.17, Ev.Matt.13.33, al., J.AJ9.4.5

σεῖσις.definition: shaking, Aret.CA2.2; concussion of the spine, Gal.18.496, al

σεῖστρος.definition: yellow-rattle, Rhinanthus major, growing in the Scamander, Arist.Mir.846a34, cf. Ps.-Plu.Fluv.13.2

σέλμα.definition: the upper planking of a ship, deck; generally, seat, throne, A.Ag.183

σημασία.definition: the giving a signal or; indication, Arist.Pr.919b36; designation, Str.8.6.5

σηπεδών.definition: decay, putrefaction, in; of live flesh, mortification, of two kinds, when a humour discharges, and when it is dry, Hp.Epid.5.4

σήπιον.definition: bone of the sepia or cuttle- fish, pounce, Arist.HA524b24, 532b1, APo.98a21

σής.definition: gen. (as if fr. which is given as; metaph., or of the Grammarians, bookworms, AP11.322 , 347

σήψ.definition: gen. putrefying sore; Arist., Thphr. , Lucan.9.723:—a serpent, the bite of which causes intense thirst, Arist.Mir.846b11, Thphr.HP9.11.1 , etc.; Nic.Th.147; mortification followed, Ael.NA16.40

σῆψις.definition: Dor. fermentation; the process by which the intestines reject that part of food which is not nutritious, opp. Arist.GA762a14, cf. Ath.7.276d, and v. II.4

σιαλίς.definition: a kind of bird, Did. ap. Ath.9.392f

σίαλος.definition: fat, grease, Hp.Acut.37 codd. MV, but is prob. to be restored fr. Erot. and Gal

σιγέρπης.definition: one that steals silently to a place, Call.Epigr.45.6

σιγύνης.definition: spear, Hdt.5.9, Opp.C.1.152; also; among the Ligyes near Marseilles was used for Hdt. l.c

σίδη.definition: = pomegranate tree and fruit, Emp.80; a water-plant growing near Orchomenos in Boeotia, = Thphr.HP4.10.1, Nic.Th.887. in signf. I, ib.72,870, etc.; but in signf. I, Emp. l.c., and in signf. II, Nic.Th.887; cf

σιδιωτόν.definition: medicine prepared from or with Paul.Aeg.6.22

σίκη.definition: or = Lat. sica, in dat. pl. mentioned as Latin by J.AJ20.8.10

σίλβη.definition: cake made of barley, sesame, and poppy-seed, Id

σιμότης.definition: the shape of a snub nose, opp; metaph., the upward curve of the tusks of a wild boar, Id.Cyn.10.13

σίνις.definition: pr. n. the Destroyer, a famous robber of the Isthmus of Corinth, E.Hipp.977, Marm.Par.36, X.Mem.2.1.14, etc.; cf

σίνος.definition: hurt, lesion, in pl., Hp.Fract.10; of things, mischief, bane, plague, used by A. alone of Trag., the mischief is revealed, Ag.389 ; ruin to them, ib.561; of Helen, ib.734 ; pest, of the , Arist.HA548a9; Thphr.CP2.7.5.…

σίξις.definition: hissing, such as is made by plunging hot metal in water, Arist.Mete.369b17

σίον.definition: water parsnip, Sium angustifolium; water pimpernel, Veronica Anagallis, Crateuas ap.Dsc. l.c

σιτονόμος.definition: dealing out corn or food, the hope of getting food, S.Ph.1091

σῖτος.definition: heterocl. pl. Xenoph.2.8; food made from grain, bread, opp. flesh-meat, Od.9.9, 12.19, cf. Hdt.2.168; a general epith. of men as opp. to beasts, Od.8.222, cf. 9.89; of savages, who eat flesh only, Hes.Op.146; of civil…

σκαλίδρις.definition: a speckled waterbird, prob. redshank, Scolopax calidris, Arist.HA593b7

σκαλμός.definition: pin or thole to which the Greek oar was; a bank or bench of rowers, Plb.16.3.4

σκάμμα.definition: that which has been dug; action of digging, Apollod.Poliorc.145.5

σκαρῖτις.definition: stone coloured like the fish Plin.HN37.187

σκαῦρος.definition: Lat. scaurus, with deviating hoof, Hippiatr.14, 104

σκάφος.definition: digging, hoeing, the time for hoeing vines, Hes.Op.572; Gp.3.4.5

σκελεαγής.definition: with broken legs, gloss on Porph.ad Il.8.402 p.300 S.; fracture of the legs, Gloss

σκέλος.definition: leg from the hip downwards, only once; as a military phrase, retreat with the face towards the enemy, retire leisurely, E.Ph.1400, Ar.Av.383; cf. 1.6b

σκέμμα.definition: subject for speculation; speculation, Pl.Cri.48c; Arist.Pol.1285b37

σκῆπτον.definition: = only in Dor. form and compds

σκῆψις.definition: pretext, plea, excuse; plea in a lawcourt, IG22.1629.205

σκίαινα.definition: a sea-fish, prob. either Corvina nigra or Umbrina cirrosa, Arist.HA601b30

σκίγγος.definition: or skink, a kind of lizard found in; = Ps.-Dsc.4.144

σκίμπους.definition: small couch, pallet, Ar.Nu.254; a kind of hammock used by invalids travelling, Gal.6.150

σκινθός.definition: diver, Thphr.HP4.6.9 ; rendered naufragus by Plin.HN13.137

σκίρον.definition: the large white sunshade which was held by the Eteobutadae over the heads of the priestess of Athena and the priests of Poseidon and Helios in the procession from the Athenian Acropolis to a place called or in a festi…

σκίρωσις.definition: induration, cirrhosis, Sor.2.36 , Gal.11.726 ; scirrosis, = duritia sine dolore, Gloss

σκόλιον.definition: prop. neut. of , song which went round crookedly at banquets, being sung to the lyre by the guests one after another in irregular order, the singer holding a myrtlebranch passed to him by the previous singer, Ar.Fr.22…

σκόροδον.definition: contr. , garlic, Allium; the garlic-market, Eup.304

σκορπίς.definition: a sea-fish, prob. Scorpaena porcus, Arist.HA543b5 ; cf

σκότος.definition: in Il. always of the darkness of death, mostly in phrase 4.461, al.; 5.47, 13.672; so in Trag. and Com., E.Hipp.837 ; Id.Ph.1453; Pherecr.40; Ar.Fr.643

σκυτάλη.definition: staff, cudgel, club, D.S.3.8; at Sparta, staff or baton, used as a cypher for writing dispatches, a strip of leather being rolled slantwise round it, on which the dispatches were written lengthwise, so that when unrol…

σκῶλος.definition: = pointed stake; metaph., evil, ruin, LXX2 Ch.28.23

σκωπαῖος.definition: v.l. among the Sybarites, a dwarf, Timae. ap. Ath.12.518e; cf

σμήρισμα.definition: air-tight fitting; tube with another inside it as in a siphon or syringe, HeroSpir.1.6,2.17

σμῦρος.definition: a kind of eel, different from Arist.HA543a24

σμῶδιξ.definition: weal, swollen bruise, caused by a blow, Il.2.267; . . 23.716, cf. Opp.H.2.428

σόγκος.definition: in Lat. form, soncus niger, = II, Plin.HN22.88

σόγχος.definition: sow-thistle, Sonchus aspera, Antiph.226.4; milkweed, Sonchus oleraceus, Ps.-Dsc.2.131

σολοιτύπος.definition: hammering a mass of iron; forged at Soli in Cyprus, Id

σόος.definition: Ep. and Ion. form of v

σορός.definition: vessel for holding human remains, cinerary; as nickname of an old man or woman, Ar.V.1365, Macho ap.Ath.13.580c

σοῦς.definition: upward motion, a Democritean term, Arist.Cael.313b5; Lacon. for acc. to Pl.Cra.412b

σκίδνημι.definition: collat. form of , disperse; mostly Pass. only pres. and impf., to be spread or scattered, disperse, freq. of a crowd or assembly, Il.1.487; Od.1.274; Il.19.277; 24.2; Od.2.252; ib.258; of foam or spray, Il.11.308; of …

σκιόπρῳρον.definition: tent or awning on the prow, ibid

σκιρτάω.definition: Ion. Opp.C.4.342:—Frequentat. of; metaph., to be skittish, unruly, E.Fr.362.31, Pl.R.571c, etc

σκοπελίζω.definition: plant boundary-stones on a man's land to warn him against tilling it, Ulp. in Dig.47.11.9:—hence ibid

σκόπελος.definition: prop. lookoutplace: hence peak, headland; watch-tower, PLips.70.2 , etc

σκοπή.definition: = lookout-place, watchtower; look-out, watch, A.Supp.786 , cf. Lyc.1311; D.S.3.26, cf. Luc.Hist.Conscr.29

σκοπιάζω.definition: poet. Verb, almost always pres. and; watch for shoals of fish, applied to certain members of a guild of lsis-worshippers, IGRom.1.817.8

σκόπιμος.definition: suitable to a purpose, Iamb.Comm. Math.7, Procl.in Alc.p.9 C., in Prm.p.487 S., Simp.in Ph.882.2

σκοροδίζω.definition: does with garlic, prop. of game-cocks which; flavour with garlic, . . Diph.17.13

σκορπίζω.definition: fut. LXXJb.39.15:— scatter, disperse; disintegrate, reduce to powder, Zos.Alch.p.177 B

σκοτάω.definition: = Ep. 3pl. their sight is darkened, Nic.Al.35

σκύζομαι.definition: Ep., used mostly in pres.: impf. Q.S.3.133, 5.338: Ep. aor. opt. Od.7.306:—to be angry with one, Il.4.23; 24.113; Od.23.209: abs., to be wroth, Il.8.483, cf. 9.198

σκυλήτρια.definition: she who strips a slain enemy, Lyc.853 codd

σκύτινος.definition: leathern, made of leather; metaph., of skin and bone, gannt, AP11.361

σκυτίς.definition: Dim. of D.L.4.56; leather amulet, Artem.5.26, cf. Afric.Cest.p.39V

σκυτόω.definition: cover or guard with leather, in Pass., IG12.313.121, 314.135; ib.22.1631.223, cf. Chron.Lind. B25; Plb.10.20.3

σκώπτω.definition: Ar.Pl.973, etc. (not in Hom., but; in good sense, joke with

σμαραγέω.definition: crash, of Zeus , Il.21.199; 2.210; resounds with the screaming of cranes, ib.463; of the battle of the Titans, Hes.Th.679; of the bowels, Hp.Mul.2.154; of Ares, Call.Del.136

σμήκτης.definition: one who rubs or cleanses, Gloss

σμήχω.definition: Hp.Acut.65, impf. Od.6.226: aor; clear off by help of lotions or salves, Dsc.1.33, 2.9, etc

σμίλευμα.definition: a piece of carved work: metaph., finely carved works, Ar.Ra.819

σμυρνίζω.definition: flavour or drug with myrrh; intr., to be like myrrh, Dsc.1.66

σμύχω.definition: aor. Il.9.653, AP5.253 :—Pass., aor. 1 Theoc.8.90; aor. 2 Luc.DMort.6.3: pf. Hld.7.21:— burn in a slow, smouldering fire, make a thing smoulder away : metaph. of grief, A.R.3.762; ib.446:—Pass., smoulder away, Il.22.4…

σμώγω.definition: smite, cited as etym. of EM721.23

σοβάς.definition: poet. fem. of of bacchanals; a kind of dance, Ath.14.629f

σολοικιστής.definition: one who speaks incorrectly, commits solecisms, title of a dialogue by Luc

σπαδονίζω.definition: metaph. in trans. sense, curtail, cramp, emasculate their sound, of the short vowels, D.H.Comp.14

σπάθη.definition: any broad blade, of wood or metal; flat wooden blade used by weavers in the upright loom used in the horizontal), for striking the threads of the woof home, so as to make the web close, A.Ch.232, Philyll.12, Pl.Ly.208…

σπαθίας.definition: like a the broad ribs, Opp.C.1.296

σπαθίζω.definition: stir with a spatula; play with the sword, v.l. in Cratin.219

σπάνις.definition: craving, defined as Stoic.3.97; D.19.153, cf. Phld.Lib.p.45 O

σπάραγμα.definition: piece torn off, shred, fragment; tearing, rending, E.Ba.739

σπαργάω.definition: = to be full to bursting, swell, be; swell with humours, . . Hp.Epid.2.6.21, cf. Gal.19.82

σπαρίζω.definition: = but formed from acc. to Lex.Rhet.ap. Eust.416.37, cf. 947.13

σπάσμα.definition: sprain or rupture of muscular fibre; spasm, convulsion, Arist.Pr.885a6

σπάω.definition: S.Ant.1003, Ar.Pax498, etc.: fut; of a sword, draw, mostly in Med., Od.22.74; . . Il.16.473; . . 19.387; PTeb.48.19 , cf. 138 : in Act., E.Or.1194; Id.IT322:—Pass., having their swords drawn, X.An.7.4.16; Id.Cyr.7.5.2…

σπένδω.definition: Il.11.775, etc.; Ep. subj. 2sg; rarely without the religious sense, simply pour, as remedy for convulsions, Hdt.4.187: metaph., AP7.555b , IG14.1957, al.; AP9.184

σπέρχω.definition: Il.13.334, etc. (Act. only in pres. and; metaph., to be hasty of temper, Il.24.248, cf. Hdt.3.72; Id.1.32; in haste and heat, Pi.N.1.40; be not hasty, E.Med.1133; Call.Del.60; to be angry with one, Hdt.5.33, Call.Del.158

σπεύδω.definition: Ep.inf. Od.24.324: fut; trans., set going, urge on, hasten, Il.13.236; Od.19.137, cf. Hdt.1.38; ib.206; E.Ion1226; procure quickly, get ready, Sol.39; E.IT1352; SIGl.c

σπίζω.definition: pipe, chirp, of the shrill note of small birds, = Arat.1024, Thphr.Sign.39

σπληνίτης.definition: of or due to the spleen; disease of the spleen, ap.Gal.18.145

σπογγίτης.definition: of, in, or like a sponge: only fem. of a stone, Plin.HN37.182; Aët.4.25, prob. in 6.80, 9.41

σποδέω.definition: pound, smite, crush; = Ar.Ec.942, 1016:—Pass., of the woman, ib.908, Th.492; of boys, Id.Ec.113

σποδιάς.definition: bullace, Prunus insititia, Thphr.HP3.6.4; quoted in form by Ath.2.50b

σποδίζω.definition: roast or bake in ashes; intr., to be ash-coloured, Dsc.5.152

σποδίτης.definition: bread baked in hot ashes, Hp.Mul.2.118, Diph.26: , = libum, Gloss

σποδοκράμβη.definition: cabbage-ash, crude potash water, Zos.Alch.p.226 B

σπονδή.definition: drink-offering, of wine poured out; esp. the Truce of God during the Olympic games, etc., Th.5.49; ibid.; during the Eleusinian mysteries, Aeschin.2.133, IG12.6.48, 68, al

σποράζω.definition: scatter, tear asunder, , of a lion, IG2.2836

στάζω.definition: Hippon.57, etc.: fut. LXXJe.49.18; c. acc. rei, drop, let fall or shed drop by drop, . . Il.19.39, cf. 348,354; Pi.N.10.81; A.Ch.1058; E.Ba.620 , cf. Tr.1199; Id.Ph.230 ; Id.Hipp.122 ; esp. of tears, Id.IA1466; Id.HF1…

σταθμόομαι.definition: = form an estimate, judge or conclude by or from a thing, freq. in Hdt. in aor. 1, c. dat., 7.11,214; . . , . . , conclude by a thing that . . , 3.15,38, 4.58 in 2.2, 9.37, 2.150, 7.237, 8.130); cf

στανύω.definition: Cret. for let them appoint an umpire city, GDI5040.66

στασιάζω.definition: intr., to be at variance, with one, X.An.2.5.28, etc.; ib.6.1.29, Pl.R.545d, etc

στατίζω.definition: poet. for place, S.Inach. in; Act. intr., stand, Id.El.316

σταφιδόω.definition: dry grapes, make them into raisins, Dsc.5.19:—Pass., Gp.5.45.4

στέγασμα.definition: anything which covers or shelters; roof, opp. Pl.Plt.279d, cf. Criti.111c

στείβω.definition: c. acc. cogn., tread or walk on a path, E.Hel.869; A.R.3.836; tread measures, E.Ion495 ; Nic.Th.609

στείνω.definition: make strait, straiten, confine, crowd; used by Hom. and Hes. only in pres. and impf. Pass., to become strait, be narrowed, Od.18.386; of persons, to be straitened for room, Il.14.34; of sheep, A.R.2.128

στείχω.definition: march in line or order , march to war, Il.2.833; 16.258; against them, Hdt.9.11; Pi.N.1.25

στελεχόω.definition: form a stem:— Pass., grow into one; metaph., bring to full growth, Id.2.456:—Pass., ib.348

στέλλω.definition: Act. intr. in sense of the Pass. , prepare to go, start, set forth, Hdt.4.147, cf. 148, 5.125, S.Ph.571,640: c. acc. cogn., . . A.Pers.609

στέμβω.definition: shake about, agitate, A.Fr.440; misuse, handle roughly, Eust.235.8

στέμφυλον.definition: mass of olives from which the

στεναχίζω.definition: or (the latter form is a freq; perh. trans. , bewail, lament, c. acc., Od.1.243

στενάχω.definition: poet. lengthd. form of only pres; Med. in act. sense, Ep. impf. Il.19.301, 23.1, al

στένω.definition: only pres. and impf.: Ep. impf. Hom. (v; after Hom., c. gen., moan or sigh for . . , E.IA370 ; also A.Pr.68; Id.Pers.295; E.Hipp.903; S.El.1180:—Med., A.Pers.62

στερέω.definition: rarely c. acc. rei, take away, AP9.174.12 : —Pass., to have taken from one, . . S.El.960 ; E.Hel.95

στερέωμα.definition: solid body, Hp.Flat.8, Anaxag. ap; immaterial solids, Dam.Pr.425, cf. 205

στερεωτής.definition: one who strengthens; title of a grade in the mysteries of Mithras, Röm.Mitt.49.206

στέρημα.definition: that which is taken away; = Ps.-Callisth.2.43

στερρόομαι.definition: Pass., in aor. opt. Hp. ap. Erot., glossed by Bacchius ibid

στεῦμαι.definition: Epic Verb, used by Hom. only in 3sg. pres. and impf., once by A. in 3sg. 1sg. cj. for in Orph.L.82, 3pl. impf. Maiist.60:—In Il. always with inf. fut., make as if one would . . , promise or threaten that one will . . …

στεφάνη.definition: anything that surrounds or; brim of the helmet, Il.7.12; 11.96; the helmet itself, 10.30, cf. Plu.2.726f

στεφανόω.definition: Med., Syracusan 2sg. imper; used by Hom. and Hes. only in Pass., to be put round in a circle or as a rim or border, and hence to be put round, round about the aegis is Terror wreathed, Il.5.739; 11.36; all round about…

στέφω.definition: encircle, crown, wreath, Hes.Op.75; S.Aj.93; E.Alc.759; Pl.R.398a; E.Ba.341; Pl.Phd.58c; Lyc.799; Call.Epigr.8, cf. AP7.657 ; Wilcken Chr.41 ii 8 :— Med., crown thy head, E.Ba.313; A.R.1.1124; Nic.Fr. 130:—Pass., to b…

στηλίς.definition: = foreg., gen. sg; a kind of number, = Iamb.in Nic.p.95P

στημόνιος.definition: of or like the threads of the warp, Thphr.HP3.18.11

στηριγμός.definition: being fixed, standing still; fixedness, of steady light, opp. flashing, Arist.Mu.395b7

στηρίζω.definition: E.Hipp.1207, etc.: fut. Hp.Morb.4.52; support, LXXGe.27.37; feed up a patient, Gal.19.192; Id.18.34, cf. Aret.CA1.1: metaph., confirm, establish, App.BC1.98; Ev.Luc.22.32, cf. 2 Ep.Thess.2.17, 1 Ep.Pet.5.10; corrobora…

στιβεία.definition: treading, walking: hence, =; tracking with hounds, D.S.4.13; cf

στιβέω.definition: tread, traverse, once in Pass., every side has been traversed, searched, S.Aj.874

στίγμα.definition: tattoo-mark, Hdt.5.35; generally, mark, spot, as on the dragon's skin, Hes.Sc.166, cf. Paus.8.2.7, 8.4.7

στιλβάς.definition: shining earth, perh. antimony or mica, Zos.Alch.p.226 B., PHolm.1.41, 2.9

στίλβω.definition: chiefly pres. and impf.: aor; metaph., shine, be bright, E.Hipp.194

στιμμίζω.definition: tinge the eyelids; later, apply any eye-salve, Aët.7.41 ; cf

στιχάομαι.definition: Ep., used by Hom. only in Ep. 3pl. impf. :—march in rows or ranks, esp. of soldiers, Il.2.92, 4.432, etc.; of ships in line, 2.516,602, etc.; of herdsmen with their herds, 18.577; of cattle, Theoc.25.126; Orph.L.272: …

στίχινος.definition: of lines or verses, of one who was rhymed to death, AP11.135

στοιβή.definition: thorny burnet, Poterium spinosum; cushion, pad, Arist.PA654b26

στοιχέω.definition: to be drawn up in a line or row; correspond, OGI458.52

στοιχίζω.definition: set in a row, esp. set a row of poles with; order or arrange in system, A.Pr.484

στολάς.definition: moving in close array; leathern jerkin, Ael.Tact.2.8

στομαλγία.definition: soreness of the mouth, ibid.: metaph., mouth-plague, i.e. incessant chattering, Id.2.101

στομάχιον.definition: dub. sens., title of a work by Archimedes

στομφάζω.definition: mouth, rant, vaunt, Ar.V.721; speak a broad dialect, Hermog.Id.1.6

στόμφαξ.definition: ranter, as Aeschylus is called by Pheidippides in Ar.Nu.1367

στόμωσις.definition: hardening of iron, making it into; surgical opening, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.10.4, 13.4

στοναχέω.definition: trans., sigh, groan over or for, S.El.133 , cf. Mosch.3.28

στόρνυμι.definition: E.Heracl.702 ; imper. Ar.Pax844; part. Hdt.7.54, S.Tr.902; compd. Od.17.32; also , A.D.Synt.295.4; A.Ag.909, Com.Adesp.1211 , but with two, ib.9); also Aristid.1.216J., Ath.2.48d: impf. Ev.Matt.21.8: later Eust.748.31…

στοχάς.definition: an erection of stone or wood for; Adj., in a row, E.Hel.1480

στράπτω.definition: rarer and later for lighten, flash; c. acc. cogn., Orph.H.19.2; Opp.C.3.349

στρατόω.definition: in Med. and Pass., to be on a campaign, in the field, Il.3.187, 4.378; A.R.2.387; assembled as a host, A.Ag.133 : contr. glossed Hdn.Gr.1.442

στρεφεδινέω.definition: spin, whirl round:—Pass., spin round and; intr. in Act., spin, whirl round, Q.S.13.7. cf

στρέφω.definition: Il.23.323, etc.; Dor. IG12.92.6; cause to rotate as on an axis, i.e. on the potter's wheel, Sannyr.4; Hdt.5.12; . . Pl.Plt.269e, cf. Epin.977b

στροβίλη.definition: plug of lint twisted into an oval shape like a pinecone, Hp.Fist.3

στρόμβος.definition: a body rounded or spun round: hence; top, Il.14.413; Luc.Asin.42

στροφαλίζω.definition: lengthd. form of twist the wool, i.e. spin, Od.18.315; AP6.218.8

στροφάς.definition: the Drifting Isles, a group not far from Zacynthus, supposed to have been once floating, Apollod.1.9.21, Str.8.4.2, St.Byz

στροφάω.definition: turn hither and thither, . . v.l. for in Nonn.D.48.381

στρόφος.definition: twisted band or cord; women's girdle, A.Th.872 ; prob. for Id.Supp.457

στρυφνόω.definition: act as an astringent; metaph. of style, make harsh, Eust.1181.27

στρώτης.definition: one that spreads, esp. one that gets ready the beds and dinner couches, Heraclid.Cum.5, Plu.Pel.30

στρωφάω.definition: poet. and Ion. Frequentat. of turn; intr., for A.R.3.893, cf. Orph.Fr.285.46

στυγέω.definition: in aor. 1, make hateful, then would I make my courage and my hands a hate and fear to many a one, Od.11.502: but this aor. is used in the common sense by A.R.4.512, AP7.430

στυρακίζω.definition: ) thrust with the butt end of; ) to be like the gum of the storax, esp. in smell, Dsc.2.84

στυφελίζω.definition: generally, treat roughly, maltreat, Il.21.380,512, Od.18.416; A.R.1.273.—Ep. word, used by Pi.Fr.225, S.Ant.139 ; also Hp.Fract.31: in late Prose, Plu.Nob.9

συγγαμέω.definition: marry together or at the same time, S.E.M.10.99, Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.51 B., Zos.Alch.p.153 B

σύγγαμος.definition: united in wedlock, married, to; generally, connected by marriage, E.Ph.[428]

συγγενής.definition: congenital, inborn, Pi.O.13.13; of the same kin, descent, or family, akin to, Hdt.1.109, 3.2, E.Heracl.229: abs., akin, cognate, A.Pr.14; E.Andr.887; S.OC1387; most nearly akin, Is.11.17; A.Pr.855; of animals, Arist.H…

συγκαθίζω.definition: make to sit together or in a body; intr. in Act., sit together, Lib.Or.11.216

συγκαλέω.definition: fut. Hom.Epigr.14.8, Att; call to council, convoke, convene, Il.2.55, A.Supp.517, Hdt.1.206, Ar.Av.201, X. l.c., etc.; Ar.Lys.22; Luc.Vit.Auct.1:—Med., Hdt.2.160, Ev.Luc.9.1, etc

συγκαταλέγω.definition: lay down with, pres. wrongly inferred from etc., v; repeat or quote along with

συγκηρέω.definition: inf. f.l. for or for in Cat.Cod.Astr.8.119

συγκλίνω.definition: lay together:—Pass., lie with; intr. in Act., lean, incline, Plb.7.11.4

συγκλονέω.definition: dash together, confound utterly, Il.13.722; AP9.755; . . , Eus.Mynd.12; EM378.48; of concussion of joints, Gal.7.185

συγκομιδή.definition: of harvest, gathering in; in pass. sense, being gathered together, crowding, Th.2.52

συγκρίνω.definition: bring into combination or aggregation; combine, Cat.Cod. Astr.2.164

συγκτίζω.definition: join with another in founding or colonizing; well cultivated, Str.4.6.9

συγκύπτω.definition: bend forwards, stoop and lay heads together; draw together, X.An.3.4.19, cf. 21

συγκυρέω.definition: aor. and :—come; c. part., like happened to be running, Emp.53; . . whether it fell in the way by chance, Hdt.8.87

συγξαίνω.definition: card wool with or together, Crates Theb.Fr.3 D

συγξύω.definition: shred or grate up, Hp.Haem.3: metaph., having scraped together every penny, D.L.4.47

συγχαλάω.definition: relax with or at the same time, Archyt.1

συγχέω.definition: Hom. uses pres. and impf. Act. and 2sg. aor; obliterate, demolish, Hdt.4.127; Id.7.115; E.Ion615

συγχρῴζω.definition: give the same colour to; Pass. also, to be closely joined, Com.Adesp.285, D.H.Comp.23

συζυγέω.definition: draw together in a yoke, to be yoke-fellows; of soldiers, stand in one rank, Plb.10.23.7; stand next in rank, Arr.Tact.7.2, 8.2

συζῶ.definition: imper. Philem.p.69 Demiańczuk:—live with; abs., live together, Pl.Plt.302b, cf. Arist.EN1126b11, 1170b11, al., Pol.1278b21, 1280b38; Id.EN1157b7

συκίζω.definition: fatten with figs, in Pass., AP9.487 ; cf

συκοφορεῖον.definition: basket for carrying figs, Gloss.: also ib

συλαγωγέω.definition: carry off as booty, lead captive; rob, despoil, Aristaenet.2.22

συλάω.definition: impf. contr. in Ep. Il.6.28; in full, c. acc. pers. et rei, strip off from another, strip him of his arms , Il.15.428, cf. 16.500; . . 6.71; E.IT157 ; D.24.182:— Pass., c. acc. rei, to be stripped, robbed, deprived of…

συλεύω.definition: Ep. form of only pres. and impf; steal away, AP5.230

συλέω.definition: rescue, a formula in the manumission of slaves at Delphi, GDI1686.11, etc

σύλη.definition: or the right of seizing the ship; is the cargo seized in IG9.333.5 : = booty, Str.17.1.8; booty, SIG10

συλλαβή.definition: conception, pregnancy; grip, hold, in wrestling, metaph., Simp.in Cael.354.5; so perh. mental grasp, participation, Phld.Mus.p.103 K

συλλέγω.definition: aor. Ar.Ra.1297, etc.: pf; Pass., come together, become customary, X.Cyr.1.4.3

συλλήγω.definition: come to an end together; have the same termination, A.D.Synt.168.13

συλλογή.definition: gathering, collecting, Th.3.111; raising, levying of soldiers, X.An.1.1.6

σύλλογος.definition: assembly, concourse, meeting of persons; metaph., collectedness, presence of mind, E.HF626

συλλοχία.definition: place where soldiers were collected into metaph., Hp.Oct.12

συμβάλλω.definition: fut. aor. inf. pf. aor. 1 Pass. these tenses Hom. uses only pres. Act., aor. Act. and Med., but most commonly Ep. intr. aor. forms Med. subj. 2sg. prob. cj. for in Il.20.335, 3sg. contr. Od.7.204:-throw together, dash…

συμβαρέω.definition: weigh down, oppress together, in Pass., Heph.Astr.3.10inCat.Cod.Astr.8.152

συμβίωσις.definition: living with, companionship; good fellowship, camaraderie, Cic.Att.13.23.1

συμβλέπω.definition: observe at the same time, Phld.Sign.36

σύμβουλος.definition: adviser, counsellor, in public or; at Athens, the were empowered to appoint , Id.58.27

συμβύω.definition: cram or huddle together, in Pass., Ar.V.1110

συμμάρπτω.definition: seize or grasp together, . . Il.10.467; Orac. ap. Od.9.289, cf. E.Cyc.397

συμμαχέω.definition: aor. IG22.10 A 7 : pf. SIG588.61 :—to be an ally, to be in alliance, A.Pers.793, Th.1.35, 7.50, etc.: c. acc. cogn., IG l.c.: c. dat., SIG366.8 , etc.; join not in war but in doing wrong, Th.1.39: generally, help, suc…

συμμαχία.definition: Ion. alliance, offensive and; generally, the duty of an ally, A.Ag.213

συμμεθύω.definition: get drunk together with, Phan.Hist.13, Heraclit.Ep.7.3

συμμετάγω.definition: carry away together, Eust.ad D.P.p.75.32 B

συμμετρέω.definition: measure jointly or in company; include in the reckoning, Agathem.5.24, 3.10

συμμηνία.definition: period when the moon does not shine, Peripl. M.Rubr.46 codd. : pl., Theo Sm.p.194 H

σύμμηνος.definition: colleague on the monthly committee of Supp.Epigr.4.535.16, 536

συμμητιάομαι.definition: take counsel with or together, Il.10.197

συμμογέω.definition: share suffering with, Opp.H.5.567; toil with, Q.S.5.105

συμμοιράω.definition: impart at the same time: things allotted, destiny, M.Ant.2.5

συμμορία.definition: taxation-group of citizens at; a division of the Athenian fleet, X.HG1.7.30

συμμορφή.definition: common or general aspect of disease, Aret.SA2.6; ib.11, cf.9

συμπαθέω.definition: to be sympathetically affected; c. dat. pers., sympathize with, Epicur.Sent.Vat.66

συμπαίω.definition: dash together or against; intr., E.Hec.116

συμπεδάω.definition: pf. Phld.Po.Herc.994.33:—bind; metaph. of frost, benumb, v.l. for X.An.4.4.11

συμπεράω.definition: cross a river together, Lex. ap. Plot. de Pulchr.p.134 Creuzer

συμπήγνυμι.definition: and (Arist.Resp.472a34; Pass., with pf. 2 to be compounded, Anaxag.4, Pl.Ti.46b; of the human frame, Hp.VM20, Them.Or.21.249c

συμπηλόω.definition: close up with clay, Zos.Alch.p.226 B

σύμπηξις.definition: putting together, constructing; condensation, coagulation, Hp.Aër.19; Arist.Mu.394a35

συμπίτνω.definition: poet. for fall or dash together, of; concur, Id.Ch.299; . . E.Hec.1029 ; ib.846; . . meets me exactly here, ib.966

συμπλαταγέω.definition: sound by striking together, clap; sound together with, Nonn.D.43.202

συμπνίγω.definition: press closely, of crowds; in Pass., to be drowned, of the Gadarene swine, Porph.Chr.49

συμπολίζω.definition: unite into one city, Pass; cover with buildings, J.BJ5.4.2

συμπολιτεία.definition: federal union of several states, with; sharing of political life, Phld.Mus.p.93 K

συμφέρω.definition: fut. A.Th.510: aor. 1; bring together, gather, collect, Hdt.7.152; Id.3.92, cf. D.24.74; Th.1.99; esp. of dead bodies, X.An.6.4.9, Lycurg.45 codd

συμφοβέω.definition: frighten at the same time, D.C.51.26:—Pass., to be afraid at the same time, Th.6.101

συμφορέω.definition: = in the primary sense, bring; metaph., of a person whose philosophy is a jumble of opinions, Epicur.Nat.14.7; cf

συμφράζομαι.definition: Med., Ep. fut. Il.9.374: pf; in later Prose Act. mention at the same time, Str.8.6.17:—Pass., to be used in the same context with, c. dat., Gal.16.706; the context, Plu.2.22a, Gal.16.707, 18.437

συμφρονέω.definition: to be of one mind with any one, agree or; think with, be in harmony with, M.Ant.8.54

σύμφυτον.definition: comfrey, Symphytum bulbosum; low pine, Coris monspeliensis, Dsc.4.9

συμψιλόω.definition: pronounce with the spiritus lenis also, in Pass., An.Ox. 1.132, EM317.46

συμψοφέω.definition: make a noise together, Plb.1.34.2; rattle upon the shields with the swords, Id.11.30.1, cf. 15.12.8

συναγείρω.definition: collect the means of living, Od.4.90:—Med., collect for oneself, 14.323, 19.293; for Il.15.680, v

συνάγνυμι.definition: aor. :—break to pieces, shiver, Il.13.166; . . , Od.14.383; . . breaks their necks, Il.11.114

συνάγω.definition: impf. Dor. A.Th.756; of persons, animals, etc., . . to the temple, Il.6.87, cf. Hdt.2.111, 3.150, etc.; Id.7.60; E.Ba.563 ; S.Fr.522; E.Or.1640, cf. Ar.Lys.585 ; crowd them into a narrow compass, Th.2.84; Pl.Phdr.256c…

συναείρω.definition: = raise up together; bind or yoke together , 10.499:—Med., 15.680

συναιρέω.definition: in Hom. only 3sg. aor. and part; bring into small compass, shorten, D.S.17.116:—Pass., to be halved, Ascl.Tact.2.1; to be contracted, Th.8.24; . . . . Plb.10.11.4

συνακμάζω.definition: blossom or flourish at the same time, of; rise to a great occasion, Plb.16.28.1

συνακούω.definition: hear along with or at the same time; understand so as to complete, S.E.M.7.239

συνακτήρ.definition: that which draws together, pair of drawers, J.AJ3.7.1

συνανάπτω.definition: fut. Pass. attach oneself to a thing, Phld.Lib.p.7 O

συνανέχω.definition: intr., rise together, Arist.Mete.372a15; abstain as well, Aret.CA2.3

συνανηβάω.definition: grow young again with or together, Them.Or.18.223c

συνανθέω.definition: blossom together, metaph; of wine, 'bloom' at the same time as, Thphr.Od.63

συνανορθόω.definition: help in correcting a text, Tz.Proll.Com.p.24 K

συναντάω.definition: meet with, encounter, c. dat., E.Ion787, Ar.Ach.1187, Pl.41,44, etc.: abs., Plb.1.52.6; E.Ion534 ; of heavenly bodies, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.204; present oneself, PCair.Zen.300.6 ; PEnteux.65.4 , cf. PCair.Zen.179.9 ; . . go…

συναντλέω.definition: drain along with, join him in bearing all his sufferings, E.Ion200

συνάντομαι.definition: only pres. and impf., poet. for fall in with, meet, abs., Od.15.538; 4.367, 21.31, Archil.89.5; Il.7.22, cf. Hes.Th.877; in hostile sense, meet in battle, Il.21.34, cf. Pi.O.2.39; satiety that accompanies not justice,…

συναπάγω.definition: lead away with or together; carry off with, . . Gal.15.638

συναπαίρω.definition: plpf. 3sg. prob. in; depart at the same time, Arist.HA597b16

συνάπειμι.definition: go away, depart together; depart or die simultaneously, Arist.Pr.862b23

συναπλόω.definition: unfold together, metaph., Hdn.Fig.p.104 S.; simplify at the same time, Dam.Pr.71:—Pass., of metal, to be beaten out together, Callistr.Stat.11

συναπορέω.definition: call in question together with; suffer poverty together, E.Fr.953.26

συναποφύω.definition: cause to branch off with, of blood-vessels, Gal.UP4.11:—Pass., ib.10.2, al

συνάρμοσις.definition: fitting together, of musical notes, Porph.in Harm.p.264 W.; = compaginatus, Gloss

συναρτύω.definition: season food as well, Xenocr. ap

συναύγεια.definition: = foreg.; esp. meeting of the rays of sight from the eye with the rays of light from the object seen, ib.4.13.11

συναυδάω.definition: speak together: hence, like agree, confess, allow, S.Aj.943, cf. Thphr.Metaph.16

συναφίημι.definition: send forth together; let loose also upon the enemy, Plb.11.12.7

συνδαΐζω.definition: fut. kill with the rest, kill also, S.Aj.361

συνδετέος.definition: to be tied or bound together; one must bind together, Paul.Aeg.6.101

συνδέτης.definition: one bound hand and foot; Act., one who binds together, Phld.Rh.1.74 S

συνδέω.definition: bind or tie together, of two or more things; of persons, bind hand and foot, Il.1.399, cf. Hdt.9.119, S.Aj.62, Ph.1016, E.Cyc.238, etc.; entangles itself, X Cyr.1.6.40:—Pass., constrained, cramped, Philostr.Im.2.21

σύνδικος.definition: one who helps in a court of; after the 30 Tyrants, judges appointed to determine disputes respecting confiscated property, Lys.16.7, cf. Harp. s.v

συνδιώκω.definition: chase away together, join in the chase; as law-term, join in the prosecution, Lex ap.D.43.57, etc

σύνδρομος.definition: running together, meeting, =; Subst., a place where several roads meet, Nearch. ap. Str.15.1.43

σύνεδρος.definition: sitting with in council, of; of birds, sitting together, friendly, Arist.HA608b29

σύνειμι.definition: have intercourse with, live with, Id.El.264, cf. E.Fr.897.7 , etc.; Ar.Pl.504, Pl.Smp.195b, etc.; live alone, X.Hier.6.2; Id.An.6.6.35, HG7.3.5; Pl.Prt.347c: also . . Ar.V.236; of fellow-travellers, Act.Ap.22.11: abs.…

συνεκβιόω.definition: live to the end along with, i.e. their not ceasing to grieve before they died, Lib.Or.2.62

συνεκδημία.definition: being or going abroad together, Gloss

συνεκρέω.definition: flow or run out along with or together, Aret.SD2.11: metaph., vanish together, Epict.Gnom.19

συνεκφέρω.definition: carry out together, esp. to burial; disgorge together, Plu.2.453d

συνελαύνω.definition: fut. Ep. aor. pf; constrain, force, Sammelb.5357.11 ; bring him to reason, ib.13 , cf. PLond.5.1711.60 ; bring to an end, PMonac.13.70

συνεξανύω.definition: D.Chr.12.43, also; equal in running, ib.298a; reach safety together with, c. dat., J.l.c

συνέξειμι.definition: go out along with or together; pass away together, Aret.SD1.4

συνεπᾴδω.definition: poet. join in celebrating; sing spells or charms at the same time, Thphr.HP9.10.4

συνεπερείδω.definition: help in driving against, c. acc. rei; Med., = Lat. conitor, Dosith.p.433 K., Gloss

συνεπέχω.definition: refer together to a thing, Iamb.in Nic.p.8 P

συνεργής.definition: working with, co-operating, Aristeas242. Adv., Phld.Oec.p.19 J

συνέργω.definition: = pres.first in Sor.1.117: fut; restrict, limit, Sor. l.c

συνερείδω.definition: press together, close; reason closely, Plu.2.600e codd

συνερύω.definition: Ion. draw together, in aor. Pass; metaph. in Act., Epigr. ap. D.L.2.112

συνηδύνω.definition: sweeten or make pleasant to the taste; generally, help in cheering, Arist.EN1126b30

συνθακέω.definition: sit with, take counsel with the night, E.Heracl.994

συνθάλπω.definition: warm thoroughly, Plu.2.974c, cf; metaph., warm or soothe by cheering words, . . A.Pr.685

συνθεσία.definition: = III, mostly in pl., covenant; nor did he forget the instructions, Il.5.319

συνθέω.definition: fut. Od.20.245:—run together with; run together, i.e. to the same place, Arist.HA533b24; Id.Cael.297a26: abs., Id.HA611a1

συνθηράω.definition: hunt together, join in the chase; catch or find together, in Med., S.Ant.433:—Pass., . . hands caught and bound together, Id.Ph.1005

συνιδιάζω.definition: give a special signification to together; intr., to be used specially with, ib.49.15

συνίημι.definition: bring or set together, in hostile sense, . . Il.1.8; 7.210; but . . shot one arrow at both together, Musae.18

συνίστημι.definition: also (Plb.4.82.5, J.BJ Prooem.5; unite Asia in dependence on himself, Hdt.1.103; bring prophetic art into union with himself, i.e. win, acquire it, Id.2.49; X.Cyr.6.1.26; Plb.2.24.6, cf. 3.42.6, 15.5.5

συννήθω.definition: aor. spin along with or together, of fate, M.Ant.4.34

συννοέω.definition: meditate, reflect upon a thing; make plans, Patrocl.1.5

συννομή.definition: a feeding together, joint pasture; the man and his allotment being a joint affair, Id.Lg.737e

συνόζω.definition: smell or be smelt together with, Arist.Pr.907a3

συνοίκημα.definition: that with which one lives, a most unpleasant house-fellow, Hdt.7.156

συνορθόω.definition: restore a ruined building along with, IG12.325.39 :—Pass., to be successful together with, Arr.An.3.9.8

συνορίνω.definition: rouse or stir up, Il.24.467:— Pass., 4.332; is stirred up, agitated, A.R.3.56

συνοχεύς.definition: one that holds together; generally, one who holds the loyalty of others, Horap.2.116

συνοχέω.definition: only in Pass., travel together in a chariot, Plu.Galb.20; Id.Ant.11

συνοχή.definition: holding together; maintenance, control, selfmaintenance, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.173; Placit.2.4.2; Epicur.Fr.361

σύνοψις.definition: a seeing all together, general view; epitome, Plu.2.1057c tit.; recapitulation, Herm.in Phdr.p.158A

συντανύω.definition: = stretch together, bringing together the strands of many matters in small compass, Pi.P.1.81

σύνταρρος.definition: interwoven, entangled, a tree with interlacing roots, ib.3.7.2, cf. 10.7

συντάσσω.definition: Att. put in order together, esp; place under command of, Arr.An.4.24.10:— Pass., metaph., Hierocl.in CA19p.461M

συντεκνόω.definition: produce or rear children with another, Stud.Pont.38 , 85 , 159

συντελής.definition: and joining in the; generally, contributory, Arist.PA674a22: cf. 11.2

συντετραίνω.definition: metaph., let the words pierce in through thy ears, A. l.c

συντίθημι.definition: used by Hom. only in Med., v. infr.:-Pass. , but is more freq. as Pass.:-place or put together, . . Hdt.2.47, cf. 4.67; X.HG2.3.20; E.IT1016; Id.Supp.1126 ; Gal.15.109; opp. fold them together, X.Oec.10.11; opp. Id.Cy…

συντρέχω.definition: fut. X.An.7.6.6: aor. 2; assemble, gather together, Hdt.8.71; Lycurg.16; run up to the rescue, Plu.Cam.27; Lat. concurrite, POxy.33 iii 8 ; PLond.1.106.19 ; Plb.2.7.6; of clouds, gather, Hdt.1.87; of liquids, is mingl…

συντυλόω.definition: in Pass., to be covered with a callus, Aët.13.133

συντυπόω.definition: help to form, Gal.5.237:—Pass., allow the soul to be moulded by circumstances, Simp.in Epict.p.69 D

συντυρόω.definition: make into cheese together: hence, comically, . . the troubles that are being concocted on their part, Ar.Eq.479

συντυχία.definition: Ion. occurrence, happening; abs. also, acc. to the context, of good or evil chances

συνωθέω.definition: force together, compress forcibly; help to propel, App.Hann.22

συνώμοτος.definition: leagued by oath: league; of things, agreed to under oath, Thom.Mag.p.346 R

συόβρωτος.definition: bitten by a wild boar, Aët.13.4 tit

συριγγίς.definition: like a pipe, i.e. quill- cassia, Androm. ap. Gal.14.73

συρράπτω.definition: sew or stitch together; metaph., put together, compose, of a treatise, Phld.Ind.Sto.4 ; form such machinations, dub. cj. for in D.C.38.14

συρράσσω.definition: Att. dash together, fight with, Th.8.96; X.HG4.3.19, cf. 7.5.16; D.S.16.4; of ships, Id.20.51; of rivers, meet with a roar, Id.17.97; . . Ph.2.513

συρρέω.definition: fut. Theo Sm.p.124 H.: pf; float along together with, Luc.Herm.86

συσκευασία.definition: packing up, getting ready, for a journey or march, ib.4.2.35

συσκηνέω.definition: live in the same tent with another, lodge; share the same berth on board ship, BGU1817.13

συσμηρίζω.definition: fit together two tubes one inside the other so as to make their contact air-tight, HeroSpir.1.28

συσπάω.definition: draw together, contract, Pl.Ti.71c; opp; draw together by stitching, sew together, X.An.1.5.10

συσσάττω.definition: stop or fill quite up, Arist.Pr.938b28, and prob. for ib.889b1

σύσσημον.definition: = signal, Aen.Tact.4.1, al; stamp on weights and measures, Str.15.1.51

συσταθμίζω.definition: weigh relatively, Ps.-Democr. ap. Zos.Alch.pp.178, 217 B.:—Med., = Iamb.in Nic.p.121 P

συστείχω.definition: aor. walk together with, c. dat., Nonn.D.4.312, al.: abs., ib.14.190

συστοιχέω.definition: stand in the same rank or line, of; correspond to, . . Ep.Gal.4.25

συστολή.definition: drawing together, drawing up; contraction, limitation, Plu.Caes.60, cf. 2.135a

σύστομος.definition: with a narrow mouth, opp; mouth to mouth, of a kiss, Telecl.12

συστροφή.definition: twisting together, to; turning round, v.l. in Placit.2.29.3, for

συστυγνάζω.definition: mourn with one, Simp.in Epict.p.90 D

σφαγή.definition: slaughter; the sg. is freq. in E., as; with collat. sense of a wound, S.Tr.573, cf. 717; . . the blood gushing from the wound, A.Ag.1389; close the gaping wound, E.El.1228 ; . . Ath.9.381a

σφάγιον.definition: victim, offering; in E. also, slaughter, sacrifice, Hec.135 ; Or.815 , cf. 658

σφάγιος.definition: slaying, slaughtering; of the throat, Max.169

σφάζω.definition: Od.4.320, Hdt.2.39, E.Tr.134 ; in Com. and Prose, from Pl. downwards, cf. title of play by Diph.,IG22.2363.34, and SIG 1024.36 ; Boeot. An.Ox.4.325: fut. E.Heracl.493: aor. Il.2.422: pf. known from plpf. D.C.73.6, 78.…

σφαιρεύς.definition: a Spartan youth, between and manhood, Paus.3.14.6, IG5.566, 674, al.; prob. from his then beginning to use the boxing-gloves

σφαιρῖτις κυπάρισσος.definition: a kind of cypress, so called from its globular fruit, Gal.12.418

σφαιρόω.definition: make into a globule; Pass., to be curled up in a ball, Ael.VH3.11

σφαίρωμα.definition: anything made round or globular; round weight, in steelyards, Arist.Mech.853b32

σφακελίζω.definition: suffer from to be gangrened; of the effect of severe cold on single limbs, to be frost-bitten, D.H.12.8

σφάλλω.definition: S.Fr.192, etc.: fut; generally, cause to fall, overthrow, Pi.P.8.15; S.El.416; . . E.Hipp.6; . . Id.Fr.31; Th.1.122, 2.87: abs., E.Hipp.262 : also of things, S.Fr.192; E.Med.198 ; Th.3.37, etc.; E.Andr.780 ; name of a…

σφάλμα.definition: trip, stumble, false step, AP7.634; a glide, in a surgical operation, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.8.38, Ruf. ib.49.28.13

σφάλτης.definition: one who trips up or throws down, Lyc.207

σφαραγέομαι.definition: burst with a noise, crackle, sputter; groan with fulness, to be full to bursting, ib.440

σφαραγίζω.definition: stir up with noise and bustle, Hes.Th.706

σφήκειον.definition: an insect that stings like a wasp, Nic.Th.738

σφηκίας.definition: = II, Pherecr.238; a verse divided by caesura into parts containing an equal number of syllables, Ps.-Plu.Metr.2

σφηκόω.definition: make like a wasp, i.e. pinch in at the; Pass., were bound tightly, Il.17.52; prob. in Antim. in PMilan.17.4; Poll.2.25; one binding up his hair, Ph.2.479; he is narrow in the neck, Nic.Th.289; is fixed, Arat.526, cf. …

σφηκών.definition: wasps' nest, cj. for sq., Arist.HA628a13

σφοδρύνω.definition: make vehement, intensify, Ph.1.355, Porph.in; intr. in Act . . Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.73

σφονδύλη.definition: an insect which lives on the roots

σφύζω.definition: Dor. only pres. and impf.:—throb, beat; beat, of the pulse, Arist.HA521a6; like the veins or arteries, Pl.Phdr.251d; Sor.2.63

σφυροτομέω.definition: bleed a person from a vessel near the ankle, Aët.8.50

σχέδη.definition: leaf, page, dub. cj. in Lex. de Spir.p.214V.; Lat. scheda is a Greek word acc. to Isid.Etym.6.14.8; cf

σχεδία.definition: Ion. raft, float; bridge of boats or pontoons, of the bridge of Darius, Epigr. ap. Hdt.4.88, cf. 97, al.; so A.Pers.68 , cf. Marm.Par.66

σχετέος.definition: what ought to be stopped, v.l. for Hp.Mul.2.133

σχίζω.definition: Hdt.2.17, S.El.99 , etc.: poet. impf; generally, part, separate, divide, Hdt.l.c., cf. 4.49; Pl.Sph.264d; Id.Ti.36b; divide them, ib.77d:—Pass., A.Ag.623; Hp.Art.20; Hdt.1.75; branches into three channels, Id.2.17, cf…

σχινίζω.definition: clean by chewing mastich-wood; Med., of certain movements in a dance, Ath.14.621c

σχίσις.definition: cleavage, parting; curdling, Id.6.694, Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.10

σχίσμα.definition: cleft, division, as of hoofs; division of opinion, Ev Jo.9.16

σχοινίς.definition: wall-decoration in form of a rope, Supp.Epigr.4.453.17 ; similar decoration of a silver cup, OGI214.55

σχοίνισμα.definition: piece of land measured out by the; generally, division, portion of a people, ib.2 Ki.8.2

σωκέω.definition: have power or strength, A.Eu.36; c. inf., to be in a condition or state to do, S.El.119

σωληνίζω.definition: hollow out like a pipe, Ruf. ap. Orib.49.27.5; cf

σωμάτωσις.definition: embodying, making of bodies, Herm; thickening, consolidation, Thphr.CP6.11.14

σωπάω.definition: Dor. and poet. for Pi.I.1.63; cf

σωρεία.definition: heaping up, Plu.Oth.14; summation, Porph.Sent.36, Iamb.in Nic.p.81 P., al

σωρευτής.definition: one who heaps up wealth, Phld.Oec.p.50 J. ; Cat.Cod.Astr.8.174, 149

σωρῖτις.definition: of Demeter, Giver of heaps of corn, Orph.H.40.5

σάφα.definition: poet. Adv. of clearly, plainly, assuredly, in Hom. esp. with Verbs of knowing, most freq. etc., like etc., to know assuredly, of a surety, followed by interrog., Il.2.192, 252, al.; by 5.183; c. acc. and interrog. cla…

σικυηδόν.definition: Adv., cucumber-like, esp. of a fracture, when the bone breaks smoothly off without splinters, Sor.Fract.10, Paul. Aeg.6.89; cf

στάγδην.definition: Adv., in drops, drop by drop, Hp.Epid.6.3.1, Aret.SA2.2

στάδην.definition: Adv., in standing posture, standing stock-still, Pl.Com.130; cf

στοιχηδόν.definition: Adv. in a row, Arist.GA770a26; line by line, following the lines, Puchstein Epigr.Gr.p.7

σύν.definition: old Att. Boeot. IG7.3171.39 : Prep. with dat. ; IPE2.383 ; ib.301 , cf. Ostr.240.5 , PLond.1.113 iv 19 ):-with. The form rarely occurs in Hom., though it is not rare in compds. even when not required by the metre, as …

συναΐγδην.definition: Adv. pressing violently or boisterously together, Hes.Sc.189

συνδιαφόρως.definition: Adv. together with a difference, Iamb.in Nic.p.13P

σύρδην.definition: Adv., dragging, in a long line; as if dragged along, violently, . . E.Rh.58; Aristid.Or.51.9

σχεδίην.definition: Ep. Adv. formed from the fem. of of; of Time, soon, Nic.Al.88; straightway, at once, Babr.57.4

σκέπανος.definition: prob. a kind of tunny, Opp.H.1.106; Dorio ap.Ath.7.322e

συνεκτέμνω.definition: excise together with, Plu.2.159c:—Pass., to be excised also, Heliod. ap. Orib.45.5.2

σπογγοτήρας.definition: sponge-watcher, a small creature like a spider which inhabits sponges, Plu.2.980b; cf

σκωριοποιία.definition: making of dross, prob. for in Zos.Alch.p.214B

συμμεταρρέω.definition: flow away together, Simp.in Epict.p.112 D

σαρκοφάγος.definition: eating flesh, carnivorous; cannibal, J.AJ13.12.6: metaph., Plu.Cat.Ma.8

συναρέσκω.definition: please or satisfy together; concede, grant, A.R.3.901, cf. 4.373

σπαναδελφία.definition: fewness of brothers or sisters, ibid., AntigonusinCat.Cod.Astr.6.71

συνηβάω.definition: pass youth together with, join in youthful sport, Anacr.24, cf. Scol.22, Opp.H.5.471; Plu.2.409a

συνέζομαι.definition: Med., sit together, in fut. inf; to be assessor, Epigr.Gr.395.4

συνεπιλέγω.definition: utter in addition; Med., read over together, Hld.10.13

σταθμόν.definition: = III.2, weight, IG12.301.21; standard weight kept under public authority, in pl., IG22.1013.10, al. ; SIG975.2

σύγκριμα.definition: body formed by combination; concert, LXXSi.35.5

συμβουλία.definition: Ion. advice or counsel; counsel, consultation, Men.Mon.355

συνδιπλόω.definition: double at the same time, Gal.19.143

συντράχηλος.definition: with head sunk between shoulders, Philostr.Gym.35

συγκτερεΐζω.definition: join in paying the last honours to a corpse, A.R.2.838

συνηρεμέω.definition: remain stationary also, of water, HeroSpir.1.2

σφύττω.definition: to be eager, c. inf., D.Chr.4.116

συμπάσσω.definition: besprinkle, bespatter, bestrew, Plu.2.89d, 638e; Sor.1.82, cf. Orib.Fr.78: also Sor. l.c

στροφεῖον.definition: twisted noose, cord, X.Cyn.2.6; machine used in the theatre in representing heroes translated to heaven or dying at sea or in war, Id.4.127,132

συμβόλαιον.definition: = mark, sign, token; in Law, contract, covenant, bond, in acknowledgement of a loan , obtain leave to bring an action for enforcing a contract, Lys.17.3; D.34.3; . . no bond with security either on bottomry or on land…

συντονία.definition: tension, of the body or its organs; tension of mind, intense application or exertion, opp. Arist.Pol.1341b41, Rh.1370a12; Pl.Def.413d

σύνοχος.definition: joined together: metaph., in; unintermittent, of fevers, Hp.Nat.Hom.15, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.10, Gal.10.603, 19.218 ; distd. fr

συνηχέω.definition: sound together or in accord; ring with, echo to, Thphr.Char.6.10, cf. Plb.2.29.6, Ph.2.153, al.:—Pass., Posidon.10 J

συγκλέπτω.definition: steal along with, Antipho6.35; deceive, elude, Hp.VC12

σκολιάζω.definition: to be crooked, walk in crooked ways, LXXPr.14.2

σπαραγμός.definition: tearing, rending, mangling; convulsion, spasm, A.Fr.169, S.Tr.778,1254; agony, Anon.Prog.inRh.1.613 W

σπόγγος.definition: any spongy substance, Hp.Steril.221; the glands in the throat, tonsils, from their spongy nature and liability to swell, Id.Epid.4.7, Gal.19.140

σκάφιον.definition: woman's chamber-pot or nightstool, Ar.Th.633, Eup.46; a fashion of haircutting , in which the hair was cut close off round the head, so as to leave it only on the crown, which then looked like a bowl, Ar.Th.838; Id.Av…

συνεξεμέω.definition: vomit out also, Arist.HA547a27:—Pass., Antyll. ap. Orib.8.5.1

στεμματόω.definition: furnish with a wreath or chaplet, E.Heracl.529

συνεπείγω.definition: help to urge on, Hp.Epid.1.8; increase or grow with, Ael.NA14.23

σύγχροος.definition: skin to skin, touching, Posidipp. ap. Ath.13.596d, Nic.Fr.32

σαρκοφυέω.definition: produce flesh, cause it to grow, Hp.Aff.38

συνεκπέσσω.definition: Att. digest, get rid of by; assist in ripening, Thphr.CP4.9.5; make mild, mellow, Plu.2.676b, al

συμπροξενέω.definition: help in furnishing with means, E.Hel.146 codd. LP, but is prob

συνδεκαδίζω.definition: celebrate the tenth day together with, c. dat., cj. in D.58.40

σύμπεψις.definition: concoction of crude humours, Gal.17.712, 18.273, Alex.Trall.4.1

σαγηνευτήρ.definition: one who fishes with the hence, of a comb, AP6.211

συνάδελφος.definition: one that has a brother or sister; member of an association, PMasp.2.11

σιτοδόκος.definition: receptive of corn or bread; Subst. keeper of corn, Hp.Epid.4.25

σαρκίδιον.definition: Dim. of a bit of flesh; = IX, Sor.1.18, Gal.14.706; of the urethral orifice, Sor.l.c

σάκχαρ.definition: Gal.12.71: also Peripl.M.Rubr.14, Orib.inc.12.6; Dsc.Eup.1.40; and Id.2.82, 107, 112:—sugar, Saccharum officinarum, ll.cc

σκαφηφορέω.definition: carry a tray of offerings at the Panathenaea, as the did, Ael.VH6.1

συνεμπυρίζω.definition: burn, consume at the same time, Supp.Epigr.6.184

συλλεαίνω.definition: Ion. pound up with; metaph., combine, in Pass., D.H.Dem.43

συννάσσω.definition: pack tight together, :-Pass., . . prob. in Supp.Epigr.7.13.7

σταφίς.definition: = I , LXXNu.6.3, al; a plant, stavesacre, Delphinium Staphisagria, Hp.Nat.Mul.95, Dsc.4.152; staphis, Plin.HN23.17

συνεποπτεύω.definition: view as an together; consider, take into account also, Sor.1.38

σιτεύσιμος.definition: of or for feeding: a fowl stuffed for the table, Lemma to AP9.484 and 486

συνεξιδρόω.definition: sweat out together, evil-smelling when exuded with the perspiration, Arist.Pr.908b34

συνταχύνω.definition: hurry on, Hdt.3.71; intr., correspond in rapidity of its course, of a disease, Ruf.Ren.Ves.Praef.2

συνοδοντίς.definition: a large kind of tunny; a fish of the Nile, Diph.Siph.ib.8.356f: hence , a stone found in its head, Plin.HN37.182

σωληνισμός.definition: hollowing out like a pipe, Ruf. ap. Orib.49.26.5

στυπογλύφος.definition: cutting, working trunks or stems, Id

συμμετοικέω.definition: emigrate or move along with, Plu.Num.21, cf. SotionParad.p.189 W

σιδηρίζω.definition: to be like iron, of the magnet, Gal.11.612; of chalybeate baths, etc., Antyll. ap. Orib.10.3.1, Paul.Aeg.1.52, 6.21

συνεργασία.definition: company or guild of fellow-workmen; a place where many slaves are lodged, a workers' barracks, Lat. ergastulum, D.S.20.13, 34/5.2.36

στύπος.definition: stem, stump, block, A.R.1.1117; pl., Plb.1.48.9, 21.27.4; also = Nic.Th.951, Al.70

συμπαρασύρω.definition: 'throw in' incidentally, Phld.Mus. p.79K., cf. p.54K

στόμφος.definition: lofty phrases, Longin.3.1: also bombast, Id.32.7

σάρμα.definition: ) sweepings, refuse, Rhinth.25, prob.l. in Heraclit.124

συζώννυμι.definition: gird together, gird up; Med. also, gird on one's armour, LXX1 Ma.3.3

σοροδαίμων.definition: a nickname of one on the brink of the grave, an old ghost, Com.Adesp.1151, cf. Plu.2.13b

σύνομβρος.definition: joined or mixed with rain, EM407.31

στόλιον.definition: Dim. of II, scanty garment, of the dress of philosophers, AP11.157 , Arr.Epict.3.23.35; v. II.2

συναλείφω.definition: anoint thoroughly, Sor.1.46, 64, al.; rub in thoroughly, Dsc.Eup.1.233

συναπαντάω.definition: come to a place at the same time, Arist.Mir.834b6, PSI6.689.9

συγκαταλύω.definition: help in undoing or putting down; intr., halt or stop for the night together, Plu.2.94a

συνδιαπνέω.definition: blow through together, f.l.in; discharge with the perspiration, Gal.18.279

σκίρτημα.definition: bound, leap, esp. of restive or frightened animals, A.Pr.675, cf. 599 ; E.HF836, cf. Hec.526, etc

σαφηνίζω.definition: make clear or plain; abs., articulate clearly, Hp.Carn.18; Arist.HA633a12, cf.Pr.888b10, 902a6

σκουτλάριος.definition: maker of scutulae for chequer-work or mosaic flooring, SIG1124

στρεπτίνδα.definition: Adv., a game in which a piece of money, shell, or the like , being laid down, was to be struck by another so as to be made to turn over, Id.9.110,117

συνεισφέρω.definition: join in paying war-tax; metaph., make gestures appropriate to his words, Lib.Or.64.74

σιτοφαγέω.definition: feed on bread, etc., Eust.ad D.P.310

στημονοφυής.definition: of the same kind with the threads of the warp, Pl.Plt.309b

σκηνοπηγέω.definition: put up a tent, set them up; keep the feast of tabernacles, J.AJ13.11.1:—Med. in Dor. form

συνοικειόω.definition: bind together as friends or kinsmen; Astrol., in Pass., to be situated together in the domicile, Vett.Val.101.5

στιχίζω.definition: in Pass., arranged in a row, LXXEz.42.3

σπαστέος.definition: to be pulled, of weeds, Thphr.HP6.5.4

συλλοχίζω.definition: embody or incorporate soldiers; arrange in order , Ael.Tact.3.2,4, Arr.Tact.5.2

σκελοτύρβη.definition: lameness in the leg, such as to make one totter about, frequent in Arabia, Str.16.4.24; acc. to Gal.19.427, a kind of paralysis

συρριζόομαι.definition: Pass., to have the roots united, Arist.de; to be rooted or founded with, Them.Or.14.183d

συγκλύζω.definition: shake up together, Dsc.Eup.1.57; metaph. in Pass., to be overwhelmed, Phld.Rh.2.303 S.; to be plunged in debt, Plu.2.831e

συνανθέλκω.definition: draw back at the same time, Herod.Med.in Rh.Mus. 58.90

συναλάομαι.definition: roam together, Man.4.290; partake in exile with any one, D.L.6.20

σαινίδωρος.definition: coaxing by presents, Epicurus' nickname for Antidorus, cj. for in Epicur.Fr.4

συνωρίς.definition: pair of horses (with or without a; generally, a pair or couple of anything, A.Ag.643; E.Med.1145, cf. S.OC895, Com.Adesp.834

σιτομέτρης.definition: one who measures and deals out; magistrate who inspected corn-measures, Hyp.Fr.271a, Arist.Pol.1299a23

σκυλεύω.definition: strip or despoil a slain enemy, esp. of his; c. acc. rei et gen. pers., strip the arms off an enemy, Lys.12.40, cf. X.An.6.1.6, HG2.4.19; . . Hdt.9.80

συνέκδημος.definition: fellow-traveller, Act.Ap.19.29; portable handbooks, vade-mecums, Paul.Aeg.Prooem.; Aët.7.103

συγχορηγέω.definition: assist with supplies; contribute towards, Id.Phoc.30

συμβαίνω.definition: fut. Hdt.2.3, etc.: pf; to be joined to them, i.e. increase them, E.Hel.37

συμπαίκτης.definition: in Lat. form senpectas , = consolers, Benedicti Regula Monachorum27, Gloss

σύναψις.definition: = contact, Arist.Ph.227a15; point or line of junction, Arist.Mech.854b39; ib.854a23; Id.PA667b8; Id.HA513b13

συνωμοτία.definition: band of sworn soldiers, file, Ascl.Tact.2.2

σωληνιστής.definition: one who fishes for the 5, Phaenias ap.Ath.3.90e

σωτηρία.definition: Ion. deliverance, preservation; in LXX and NT, salvation, LXXPs.50.14, al.; 1 Ep.Pet.1.9; Ep.Eph.1.13, etc

στιχιστής.definition: writer of verse, Id.ad Lyc.425; condemned by Thom.Mag.p.189 R

συναληθεύω.definition: to be true together, Arist.Int.19b36, cf; join in seeking or speaking the truth, Plu.2.53b

συμπροάγω.definition: lead forward together; intr., move forward with or together, Plu.Phil.21, Agis19

σύμπτυξις.definition: folding up or together, closing, Procl.Hyp.5.116; embrace, enfolding, Dam.Pr.29; ib.155

συναπαυξίφως.definition: decreasing in light together with, c. dat., Arg.Man. post Max.p.99 L

συντεχνία.definition: guild, IGRom.3.896 , Judeich Altertümer von Hierapolis 133

συναθλέω.definition: = with one, Ep.Phil.4.3; impress by practice upon, D.S.3.4

συνιζάνω.definition: sink or settle down, collapse; sink, Thphr.Od.29; of the blood, Id.Sens.43; of the wind, Luc.VH1.29

συνῳδία.definition: concord, and metaph., agreement, assent, Pl.Lg.837e, etc.: lit., Aristid.Or.18.7; of the Spheres, Iamb.VP15.65: also Onatas ap. Stob.1.1.39; concentus, Gloss., cf. Charis.p.552 K

συνεσσάδδω.definition: aor. inf. Cretan for help to remove property, Leg.Gort.3.13, 16

συνεράω.definition: pour together, gather together, Arist.GA752a4; to explain Ath.8.362e: is v.l. for in Isoc.5.138

σταφυλή.definition: bunch of grapes; = I, Thphr.HP3.18.11, Plin.HN23.21

συναποπλέω.definition: float out, be washed out together, Sor.1.73; sail away with, c. dat., Zos.4.43

συνοδίτης.definition: = Latin Comes, BGU1137.9; relating to the of sun and moon, Dam.Isid.233

συμφυσάω.definition: blow together, metaph; weld together, Pl.Smp.192d:—Pass., Arist.Cael.304a21: metaph., contrive, Ar.Eq.468

συγκαλύπτω.definition: cover or veil completely; intr. in Act., Them.Or.4.59b

συνωμία.definition: space between the shoulder-blades, withers, in the bull of Phalaris, Plb.12.25.3 ; in a horse, Hippiatr.128 ; ib.26; in a human being, Paul.Aeg.3.20; Id.6.88

σύννοος.definition: Att. contr. in deep; anxious, gloomy, Arist.Pr.958a18, cf. Hp.Ep.15, D.H.4.66, etc.; grave, Hp.Medic.1

συνεκραίνω.definition: distil at the same time, Thphr.HP3.13.2

στερέσιμος.definition: liable to be taken away, OGI515.29 , Hierocl.Facet.246; = commissum, Gloss

συκάριον.definition: Dim. of small fig, Eup.179, Gloss

συνεδρία.definition: sitting together, of birds from whose position favourable omens were drawn, A.Pr.492 ; Arist.HA608b28, cf. EE1236b10

συνολκόομαι.definition: to be displaced at the same time, of the uterus, Sor.2.29

σύμπλεξις.definition: an inclusive term, Arist.PA644a4; complexity of the pulse, Gal.9.50

στύω.definition: fut. AP10.100 : aor.1 inf. Ar.Lys.598:—make stiff or erect: sens. obsc., penem erigere, Ar. l.c.:— Pass. , Id.Av.1256; Luc.Alex.11: aor. Pass. Diog.Ep.35.3

στεφάνωμα.definition: that which surrounds, crown; a crown as the prize of victory, Pi.P.12.5; Id.I.2.15

στηλίτης.definition: fem. of or like a; inscribed on a posted or placarded as infamous, Isoc.16.9, D.9.45; Thrasyb. ap. Arist.Rh.1400a32; cf. foreg

στενόσημος.definition: with narrow border: = Lat. tunica angusticlavia, opp. Arr.Epict.1.24.12

συμφεύγω.definition: fut. E.Ph.1679:—flee along with; to be banished along with, Lycurg.25; shared in this banishment, Pl.Ap.21a

σιταγέρτης.definition: collector of corn for state purposes, commissary, Tab.Heracl.1.102, 177

συκολογέω.definition: gather figs, Ar.Pax1346; speak about figs, Ath.3.79a

συγκαττύω.definition: patch up, cobble, of shoemakers, saddlers, etc., Luc.Hist.Conscr.23, cf. Sat.28

στοιβάζω.definition: pile or heap up, pack together, LXXLe.1.7, al., Luc.Cat.5:—Pass., of a wall, to be packed, filled up, CPR232.16 ; cf

σιδηρονόμος.definition: distributing with iron, i.e. with the sword, A.Th.788

σύμψαυσις.definition: contact, Arist.PA660b24; touching of two notes together, Ptol.Harm.1.7

συμβρέμω.definition: roar along with or together, D.C.66.22

σχεδεκδότης.definition: editor, dub. cj. in Lex. de Spir.p.197 V

συνόλλυμι.definition: destroy together, Bion1.29 :—Med., perish along with, E.Hel.104

σκαιουργέω.definition: behave amiss, towards one's parents, Ar.Nu.994

συγκατασπάω.definition: pull down with oneself; gulp down, swallow together, Luc.DMort.8

σχολεῖον.definition: school, Arr.Epict.3.23.30; perh. burial place, resting-place, BCH10.414 , Supp.Epigr.4.543

συνεκφρύγω.definition: parch at the same time, Damocr. ap. Gal.13.1003

σαίρω.definition: only found in pf. with pres. sense; transferred to grinning laughter, Hp.Gland.12; Luc.Am.13: the neut. is used in Adv. sense, Theoc.20.14; of a fox, Babr.50.14, cf. Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.26

σαλάσσω.definition: overload, cram full, AP6.56 , cf. 11.57 , APl.4.306 ; cf

στύραξ.definition: storax, Mnesim.4.62; or the tree producing this gum, Styrax officinalis, fem. in Hdt.3.107, masc. in Str.12.7.3, Plu.Lys.28

σιτόλεθρος.definition: pest of corn, destruction of corn, Hdn.Epim.203

σίπυδνος.definition: collat. form of sq., Orac. ap. Luc.Alex.25

συναισχύνω.definition: begrime, soil at the same time, Max.Tyr.18.9

σάνδυξ.definition: a bright red colour, also called Str.11.14.9 ; obtained by heating , Dsc.5.88, cf. Plin.HN35.40; though a like colour was made from a plant of the same name, red sandalwood, Pterocarpus santalinus, Sosib.21, Verg.Ecl.…

στρατύλλαξ.definition: perh. Comic Dim. of toy captain, Cic. Att.16.15.3

συνδιασήπω.definition: make putrid together, Gal.7.297:—Pass., to be or become so, ib.388 = sq., Hierocl.p.54 A

σταχυηκομέω.definition: to be decked with ears of corn, of fields, Opp.C.2.150

στρεβλότης.definition: being twisted, crookedness; frowardness, perversity, Aq., Thd.Pr.4.24, Aq., Al.ib.6.14

συνάλλομαι.definition: leap together, Luc.Anach.4; of a horse; start back with terror, Artem.1.57

συοβόσκιον.definition: herd of swine, Charis. p.551 K

συναυλέω.definition: play on the flute at the same time, Luc.Dom.16, Ath.14.617b, Longus2.35

σῖγα.definition: Adv., silently, used in Trag. (and late; under one's breath, in a whisper, quietly, secretly , A.Ag.449; S.Ant.700; Id.Ph.22; Orph.A.702; . . S.OT1212

στιχισμός.definition: numbering of the lines of a book, Tz.H.9.291

συνορμέω.definition: lie at anchor with, c. dat., Plb.5.68.6, 110.2

στίχος.definition: row or file of soldiers, X.Lac.11.5,8; old name for Ascl.Tact.2.2, cf. Ael.Tact.5.2, Arr.Tact.6.1

συφεός.definition: hog-sty, Od.10.238, 14.13, 73, Parth.12.2; to the sty, Od.10.320:—Ep. form ib.389

σπηλαΐτης.definition: worshipped in grottos, of certain gods, Paus.10.32.5

συσσήπω.definition: macerate food completely, for digestion, Arist.PA675a13:—Pass., with pf. Act., grow putrid together, Hp.Loc.Hom.29, Ael.NA10.13, Porph.VP44

σύμφθαρσις.definition: simultaneous destruction; melting into one another, Hermog.Id.1.12, cf. Iamb.in Nic.p.80 P

σύκωσις.definition: ulcer resembling a fig ripe to bursting, with projecting edges, esp. on the eyelids, Cels.6.3, Gal.12.348,716, UP10.12, Sever. ap. Aët.7.45; Archig. ap. eund.8.14

σκολιότης.definition: crookedness, of a; metaph., inequality, to be unequally affected, Hp.Acut.22

στιχολογία.definition: recitation of verses, dub. ib. xiii 10

σύγχωσις.definition: filling up of trenches, Ath.Mech.16.2 ; prob. for in Plu.2.434c

συνομολογέω.definition: say the same thing with, agree with; Med., correlate, Hp.Epid.6.8.26

συναπολείπω.definition: leave behind along with; intr., fail or cease together, Thphr.CP2.19.3

συνεξόζω.definition: smell of a thing besides, Thphr.Od.60

σεμνολόγος.definition: one who speaks solemnly or affectedly, D.18.133. Adv. App.Mith.70

σύμπλοος.definition: metaph., partner or comrade in a thing, S.Ant.541

συνηλικία.definition: poet. body of comrades or playmates, Supp. Epigr.6.140.22

συμφυής.definition: born with one, congenital, natural; adapted by nature, Arist.de An.420a4; Epicur.Fr.30, cf. Ep.1p.14U

συγκαίω.definition: Att. set on fire with or at; overheat, inflame, Hp.Aër.9; Id.VM10, cf. Gal.15.559:—Pass., Prodic.4; in Act., liable to inflame, Id.Aër.7

σέλαγος.definition: ray, . . Hymn.Is.30: nom. pl. dub. in Tryph.428

σύμψηφος.definition: voting with, Pl.Grg.500a, cf; = computator, Gloss

συναναφλέγω.definition: set fire to along with or together, Ph.1.345, v.l. for in 2.27

συνωρίζω.definition: yoke together, Ael.NA15.24:—Med; intr., to be yoked together, Nic.Fr.74.23, Man.4.453

στιβευτής.definition: = foreg. II, Sostrat. ap.Stob.4.20.70;= vestigator, Gloss

στρεψίκερως.definition: an African antelope with twisted horns, the addax, Plin.HN11.124

συνεισπέμπω.definition: send into along with, Ael.VH12.43 codd

σκιατραφής.definition: brought up in the shade, i.e. leading a sedentary life, Agath.1.7

συνεθίζω.definition: intr. in Act., grow accustomed, . . Epicur.Ep.3p.64U., cf. p.60 U

σφάκελος.definition: gangrene, mortification, or, of bones; generally, spasm, convulsion, A.Pr.878 ; E.Hipp.1352 : metaph., the convulsive fury of winds, A.Pr.1045

συνεπῳάζω.definition: sit on eggs together with, Arist.HA555b14

σηματουργός.definition: one who makes devices for shields, A.Th.491

στιγματίας.definition: in Com., one whose property is marked as mortgaged, Cratin.333

σελάχιος.definition: of fishes, cartilaginous, having no scales, Artem.2.14, Ar.Byz.Epit.1.21, 111.10

συνεκβιβάζω.definition: causal of help in bringing out, sc. from the mud, X.An.1.5.7

στοργή.definition: love, affection, Emp.109.3, AntiphoFr.73; rarely sexual love, AP5.165 , 190 , 7.476

συνολκή.definition: contraction, of circles, Hierocl.p.62 A; spasm, Id.ib.8.5.1; in tetanus, Aret.SA1.6; hysteric convulsions, Sor.2.26; cramp, Gal.14.736

συμφράδμων.definition: one who joins in considering; harmonious, in accord, AP9.365 ; A.R.Fr.8

σχολαστής.definition: one who lives at ease, man of; as Adj., leisurely, idle, Id.Cic.3,2.135b; Id.Sol.22

συνεκτρέχω.definition: aor. run out along with or; Astrol., of the moon in conjunction, not yet having abetted the sun's rays, Heph.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.158

σταμνίας.definition: Com. pr. n., Wine-jar, prob. formed like Ar.Ra.22

συμπαράγω.definition: help to move sideways; lead alongside, D.S.14.59

στελεχιαῖος.definition: forming a trunk: the vena portae, from which all the others were supposed by the ancients to branch, Gal.2.574, 8.413

σχίζα.definition: piece of wood cut off, lath; shaft, dart, LXX1 Ki.20.20 sq., 1 Ma.10.80, AP6.282 ; so IG22.1629.996

σκότωσις.definition: darkening, eclipse; dizziness, vertigo, Stoic.3.57, Erot. s.v. Gal.19.417: metaph., Porph.Sent.29

σποδός.definition: wood-ashes, embers, Od.9.375, h.Merc.238; dust, Hdt.4.172; of labour in vain, Arr.Epict.3.26.17

σιτόκουρος.definition: consuming bread and doing nothing else, wastrel. Alex.177, Men.244, 420

σαθέριον.definition: prob. a kind of beaver, Arist.HA594b31

σωματόω.definition: make corporeal, prob. in Philol.11:—Pass; Pass., to be embodied, associated with a body, . . Plot.1.6.5; Dam.Pr.16

σκαληνόομαι.definition: Pass., have the conception or impression of something unequal or crooked, Plu.2.1121b
